reader noun

a person who reads

also readers, dear reader, the reader

classical

Cic. Fam. 5.12.4: ad dēlectātiōnem lēctōris (Lewis & Short)
Hor. Ep. 2.1.214 (Lewis & Short)
Phaedr. 4.7.21

1lēctor: long e (Lewis & Short leaves it unmarked). From lēctus, legō: Lachmann’s law; Gellius 9.6.3 on āctitō from āctus. Ruling: Lachmann’s law: āctus, lēctus, frāctus.

lēctor1, lēctōris m.

noun, third declension · Declension on Wiktionary

a reader

The reader of a book. Lewis & Short’s other senses: a slave who read aloud to his master (Quint. 2.5.6, Plin. Ep. 9.17.3), and in the Church a lector (Tert.). The long ē by Lachmann’s law, from lēctus.

Examples

  • quid ergō possum facere tibi, lēctor Catō, sī nec fābellae tē juvant nec fābulae?

    So what can I do for you, my Catonian reader, if neither little stories please you nor big ones?Phaedr. 4.7.21–22

See also read, book, author.
